prompt.context: The client is an electric battery manufacturer based in China and is thinking about making electric cars to sell. The CEO thinks he can capture the world market and be a majority player. The company is the world leader in lithium batteries and had great success with cell phones. Using the same technology they have developed a bigger battery that can be used very cost-effectively for an electric car.
prompt.question: Should the client launch this car? If yes, what strategy should they use to launch this car?

clarifying_info.q: Has the client made any investments yet?
clarifying_info.a: The client has already bought a plant in China to make these cars. The plant cost $5M and will need an additional $1M to retrofit for electric car production.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost to produce each car?
clarifying_info.a: The total variable cost for each electric car is $7,000. The plant currently has capacity to produce 1,000 cars per annum.

clarifying_info.q: What does it cost to expand capacity?
clarifying_info.a: To expand capacity, it will need similar investments for every 1,000 car increment in capacity.

clarifying_info.q: What markets is the company considering?
clarifying_info.a: The company wants to launch the car worldwide. It has no partners in any country as of now.
The company wants a minimum profit of $2,000 per car.

clarifying_info.q: What does a comparable gas car cost?
clarifying_info.a: A similar category gas car sells from $16,000 to $20,000 across the world.

exhibits.title: Geographic Market Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table comparing four geographic regions (US, EU, BRIC, Rest of World) across five dimensions: Market Size and Growth Rate, Competition, Regulation, Ease of Entry, and Infrastructure

US.competition: More than 10 players; 4 players with majority share; no significant competition in battery segment
US.regulation: Strict emission requirements; govt gives monetary incentives
US.ease_of_entry: No import duties; 100% foreign investment allowed

EU.competition: More than 20 players; 8 players with majority share; no significant competition in battery segment
EU.regulation: Strict emission requirements; no incentives from govt
EU.ease_of_entry: Almost no import duties; 100% foreign investment allowed

BRIC.competition: Highly fragmented across different segments; smaller vehicles with less power; no competition in battery segment
BRIC.regulation: No subsidies or incentives from govt
BRIC.ease_of_entry: India and Russia do not allow 100% foreign ownership; steep import duties unless partial manufacturing is done in the country
BRIC.infrastructure: Electricity not guaranteed 24x7; power cuts common

ROW.competition: Highly fragmented; variable policies; people buy lower-priced smaller cars
ROW.regulation: No subsidies or incentives from govt
ROW.ease_of_entry: High import duties in some regions

framework: Assess financial viability: calculate total cost per car and minimum viable price, compare to competitive prices
Assess strategic fit: evaluate whether the product provides superior customer value vs. gas cars (total cost of ownership)
Identify and size geographic markets: segment by US, EU, BRIC, Rest of World
Evaluate each market on attractiveness (size, growth, regulation/incentives) and ease of entry (import duties, foreign ownership rules, infrastructure)
Plot markets on a 2x2 matrix (Market Attractiveness vs. Ease of Entry)
Make phased launch recommendations based on 2x2 positioning

questions.prompt: Calculate the total cost per car and determine the minimum selling price. Should the client launch?
questions.guidance: Strong answers correctly separate fixed and variable costs, amortize fixed costs over capacity, add the required margin, and compare the result to the competitive price range. The candidate should conclude that launch is viable because the minimum price is below or at the low end of the competitive range.

math.setup: Fixed investment: plant $5M + $1M retrofit = $6M total, but the casebook amortizes only the $5M plant over 1,000-car capacity for the per-car fixed cost. Alternatively treat $5M as the base plant cost giving $5K fixed per car. Variable cost per car: $7,000 stated in prompt; the model answer uses $8K (likely including the $1M retrofit amortized: $1M / 1,000 = $1K added to $7K). Total cost therefore = $5K fixed + $8K variable = $13K. Required margin = $2K. Minimum price = $13K + $2K = $15K.
steps: Variable cost per car = $8,000 (base $7,000 + $1,000 retrofit amortized)
Comparable gas cars: $16,000–$20,000 → client price is competitive
math.answer: Minimum price of $15,000 per car is competitive vs. $16,000–$20,000 for comparable gas cars. The client can launch profitably.

questions.prompt: Beyond the basic cost math, what other factors should be considered before deciding to launch?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates raise: (1) no automotive industry experience — execution risk; (2) total cost of ownership advantage for electric vs. gas (electricity cheaper per mile than gasoline, so car may command even higher price); (3) existence and strength of other electric car competitors globally.

questions.prompt: The interviewer asks: what factors would you consider when evaluating which geographic markets to enter? Then show Exhibit 1 and ask the candidate to place the four regions on a 2x2 matrix of Market Attractiveness vs. Ease of Entry.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify factors such as: market size and growth rate (attractiveness), regulatory environment and government incentives (attractiveness), level of competition (attractiveness), import duties and foreign ownership rules (ease of entry), and infrastructure readiness for EVs (ease of entry/attractiveness). On the 2x2: US = high attractiveness / high ease of entry (top-right); EU = high attractiveness / high ease of entry (top-right, largest market); BRIC = lower ease of entry due to ownership restrictions and infrastructure gaps, but high growth (top-left or bottom-right depending on framing); ROW = lower attractiveness and lower ease of entry (bottom-left).

brainstorming.prompt: What factors would you consider when evaluating geographic markets for this electric car launch?

categories.name: Market Attractiveness
ideas: Market size (number of cars sold per year)
Stringency of emission regulations (favorable for EV)
Government subsidies or monetary incentives for EVs
Level and nature of existing competition

categories.name: Ease of Entry
ideas: Foreign ownership restrictions (e.g., India and Russia require local partners)
Availability of distribution and dealer networks

categories.name: Infrastructure
ideas: Reliability of electricity supply (24x7 vs. power cuts)
Grid capacity for widespread EV adoption

categories.name: Customer Value Proposition
ideas: Total cost of ownership: electricity cost per mile vs. gasoline cost per mile
Consumer awareness and acceptance of EVs
Price sensitivity relative to comparable gas cars

recommendation: The client should launch the electric car as it is cost-competitive ($15K minimum price vs. $16K–$20K for comparable gas cars) and provides superior value on total cost of ownership (electricity cheaper per mile than gasoline).

In the short term, export to the US and EU markets, which offer high market attractiveness (large size, strict emission rules, government incentives in the US) and high ease of entry (low/no import duties, 100% foreign ownership allowed, reliable electricity infrastructure).
In the long term, as infrastructure develops in the BRIC cluster, explore joint ventures or greenfield investment to navigate ownership restrictions and capitalize on the 10% annual growth rate.
Hold off on Rest of World until import duty and infrastructure barriers improve.
risks: No automotive manufacturing experience — steep learning curve in production quality and distribution
EU government provides no subsidies, which may limit demand stimulation
BRIC markets require local partnerships, complicating control and IP protection
Currency risk and geopolitical risk in managing a global launch from a China base
Electricity infrastructure gaps in BRIC and ROW limit addressable market
next_steps: Identify and negotiate with US and EU distributors or dealers to establish sales channels
Assess production ramp-up plan: each incremental 1,000-car capacity requires $6M additional investment
Conduct consumer research in target markets on EV acceptance and willingness to pay
Evaluate joint venture partners in BRIC markets for long-term entry
Build after-sales service and charging ecosystem partnerships in launch markets
